replace_A2_with_Facts: [F1] [[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]: a continuous real function on a closed nondegenerate finite-dimensional rectangle is Riemann integrable.

[F2] [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]]: if a Riemann-integrable function on a product of closed rectangles has integrable sections, its ordinary iterated integrals in both orders exist and equal its multiple integral.

[F3] [[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle]]: for continuous real $g$ and its continuous parameter derivative on a compact two-variable rectangle, that derivative passes through the finite integral, including one-sided parameter endpoints.
[F4] [[lem-uniform-integral-error-bound]]: if integrable $f,g$ differ in sup norm by at most $M$ on $[a,b]$, their integrals differ by at most $(b-a)M$.
exact_proposed_body_edits.insert_after_1_1:
1.2 Here and below the coordinate integrals of smooth compactly supported functions may be computed on the closed coordinate intervals after extension by zero. This extension is smooth on a neighborhood of the closed box: compact support leaves a neighborhood of every boundary face where the function is zero. By [F1] the function and every coordinate section are Riemann integrable; [F2], applied to successive coordinate blocks, identifies all iterated orders with the same box integral. In particular, the marginal $H(x')=\int_{a_1}^{b_1}h(s,x')\,ds$ has total integral equal to $\int_\Omega h$. To differentiate a marginal, fix all other coordinates and restrict the differentiated coordinate to a compact interval inside its open side interval. The integrand and each parameter derivative are continuous on the resulting compact two-variable rectangle, so repeated [F3] gives
$$\partial_{x'}^\beta H(x')=\int_{a_1}^{b_1}\partial_{x'}^\beta h(s,x')\,ds,\qquad \sup|\partial^\beta H|\le (b_1-a_1)\sup|\partial_{x'}^\beta h|.$$
The inequality follows from [F4] with the second integrand zero. Continuity of these derivatives jointly in the remaining parameters follows from the same bound applied to their differences and uniform continuity of the integrand derivative on each compact box. The same reasoning differentiates an integral with upper endpoint $x_1$ in its other parameters. For its $x_1$ derivative, the difference quotient of $\int_{a_1}^{x_1}f(s,x')\,ds$ differs from $f(x_1,x')$ by at most $\sup_{s\text{ between }x_1\text{ and }x_1+\delta}|f(s,x')-f(x_1,x')|$, which tends to zero by continuity; higher endpoint derivatives then follow by ordinary differentiation. This proves the finite-integral identities used in the recursion. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4]
exact_proposed_body_edits.replace_3_1:
3.1 If inputs are supported in fixed compact $K$, each coordinate projection $K_i$ is compactly contained in $(a_i,b_i)$. Choose closed intervals $J_i\Subset(a_i,b_i)$ containing $K_i$ and the support of the already fixed bump $\theta_i$. Their product is a common compact output-support set $K'=\prod_iJ_i$: before the first-coordinate support the primitive is zero, and after it the primitive is zero because its full first-coordinate integral is zero; the other components have the required support by induction. Write $p_m(f)=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\sup|\partial^\alpha f|$, taking the maximum also over components for vector fields, and put $\ell_1=b_1-a_1$. Step 1.2 gives $p_m(H)\le\ell_1p_m(h)$. For the first component in step 2.1, a derivative with no $x_1$ differentiation is an integral of $\partial_{x'}^\beta h-\theta_1\partial_{x'}^\beta H$ and is bounded by $\ell_1(1+\ell_1\|\theta_1\|_\infty)p_m(h)$. If the derivative differentiates $x_1$ at least once, the endpoint identity in step 1.2 gives a derivative of $h$ minus a fixed derivative of $\theta_1$ times a derivative of $H$, again bounded by a constant times $p_m(h)$. For each remaining component $\theta_1(x_1)(R'H)_{j-1}(x')$, the product derivative is bounded by a fixed bump-derivative constant times $p_m(R'H)\le C'_m p_m(H)$ by induction. The dimension-one bounds in step 1.1 start this induction. Thus
$$p_m(Rh)\le C_m p_m(h)\qquad(m\ge0),$$
where $C_m$ depends only on the fixed rectangle, bumps, dimension and $m$, not on $h$. These are all fixed-support seminorm estimates, proving the full stated continuity. Every displayed construction is linear in $h$, and the bumps were fixed once independently of $h$ and $K$, so the same map $R$ serves all compact input supports. [given, A1, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, induction] ∎
